section_title: Conflicting Evidence, Model Limitations, and Open Questions
thesis: The 90 cross-study disagreements recorded for this review are not noise: they sort almost completely into five recurring axes - what was measured, where, in which construct, in which cohort, and under what design rigor. The single most consequential is the first: reporter-based fate mapping and stereology return small or null changes where immunoreactivity counts return large losses, and no study has applied a marker-independent identification of SST interneurons to human Alzheimer cortex.
scope_notes: Cross-cutting critical section: conflicting results, model limitations, open questions. Draws on conflicts flagged in every cluster.

findings.claim: Kainate-induced status epilepticus causes highly selective hilar neuron loss in which 83% of the missing GABAergic neurons are somatostatin-immunoreactive, while overall GABAergic loss (13%) is far smaller than mossy cell loss (52%), and lateral inhibition in the dentate is nonetheless preserved.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Interneuron loss is remarkably specific; 83% of the missing GAD-positive neurons are somatostatin-immunoreactive.
findings.evidence: Stereological counts of GAD-positive and GAD-negative hilar neurons with paired recordings of lateral inhibition in kainate-treated rats.
findings.effect_size: 52% loss of GAD-negative hilar neurons, 13% loss of GAD-positive cells, of which 83% are somatostatin-immunoreactive
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Kainate-treated rats lose an average of 52% of their GAD-negative hilar neurons (putative mossy cells) and 13% of their GAD-positive cells (GABAergic interneurons) in the dentate gyrus.
findings.study_system: Rat dentate gyrus after kainate-induced status epilepticus

findings.claim: Unbiased stereology in a transgenic AD rat model found no change in PV+, CR+ or SST+ interneuron numbers, with reduction restricted to CCK+ cells, arguing against generalised interneuron loss as an early feature.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We could not observe any change in cell numbers of the PV+, CR+, SST+ neurons in the young TgF344-AD rats.
findings.evidence: Unbiased stereological counts of PV+, CR+, SST+ and CCK+ interneurons, plus Iba-1 and GFAP cells, in hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex of young TgF344-AD rats versus wild-type
findings.effect_size: No detectable change in PV+, CR+ or SST+ cell numbers; the only interneuron reduction was in CCK+ neurons (qualitative, no numeric contrast given in this sentence)
findings.study_system: Rat (TgF344-AD), hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex, unbiased stereology

findings.claim: Sst-Cre driver lines label a minority of cells that also express parvalbumin, so Cre-based identification of SST interneurons carries a quantifiable off-target/overlap error.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the Pvalb-Cre line 2 ± 1% of labeled cells were stained by both antibodies, and in Sst-Cre mice 6 ± 3% of labeled neurons expressed both PV and SOM.
findings.evidence: Immunostaining of tdTomato-labelled cells from Pvalb-Cre and Sst-Cre reporter crosses quantified double-labelled somata; a further 7% of Pvalb-Cre tdTomato+ cells expressed neither marker.
findings.effect_size: 6 ± 3% of Sst-Cre labelled neurons PV+/SOM+ (vs 2 ± 1% in Pvalb-Cre)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In the Pvalb-Cre line 2 ± 1% of labeled cells were stained by both antibodies, and in Sst-Cre mice 6 ± 3% of labeled neurons expressed both PV and SOM.
findings.study_system: Mouse presubiculum, Pvalb-Cre and Sst-Cre tdTomato reporter lines

findings.claim: App/Psen1 knock-in mice express APP at physiological levels, explicitly avoiding the overexpression artifacts of first-generation randomly-inserted transgenic APP models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the first‐generation transgenic APP mouse models, familial AD mutations are randomly inserted into the mouse genome, and non‐endogenous promoters drive gene overexpression. 18 In our mice, the familial AD genes were knocked into the same gene locus on the mouse APP homologs.
findings.evidence: Western blot with an antibody recognising mouse and human APP showed equivalent full-length APP across knock-in and control mice at 3, 6 and 9 months, confirming physiological expression.
findings.effect_size: similar full-length APP levels in knock-in vs control at 3, 6, 9 months (no overexpression)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Western blot analysis of cortical tissues from mice 3, 6, and 9 months of age showed similar levels of FL‐APP (22C11) in both NA and NOG mice, thus confirming the lack of overexpression and physiological levels of APP gene expression in the NA mice.
findings.study_system: App/Psen1 knock-in mouse model of Alzheimer's disease, cortex

findings.claim: A 3 h postmortem interval alone generates substantial differential gene expression in neurons and obscures genuine disease-related transcriptomic changes, a direct confound for postmortem human studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In neurons, we identified 79 upregulated and 53 downregulated differentially expressed genes (DEGs; q value <0.1) at the 3 versus 0 h PMI (Fig. 2A).
findings.evidence: Single-nucleus transcriptomics of PS19 tauopathy and wild-type mouse brain sampled at 0 h versus 3 h postmortem; PMI-driven DEGs were enriched for immune and stress pathways and masked genotype effects.
findings.effect_size: 79 upregulated and 53 downregulated neuronal DEGs induced by 3 h PMI alone (FDR q<0.1)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In neurons, we identified 79 upregulated and 53 downregulated differentially expressed genes (DEGs; q value <0.1) at the 3 versus 0 h PMI (Fig. 2A).
findings.study_system: PS19 tauopathy and wild-type mice, snRNA-seq of brain at 0 h and 3 h postmortem

findings.claim: Phenotypes in APP/PS1/tau transgenic mice may arise from mutant protein overexpression rather than from the pathological lesions themselves; a human MAPT model under its native promoter showed only mild (<35%) overexpression.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The wildtype genomic human MAPT transgene is under its native promoter control [9], and when compared to wildtype mouse tau, we only observed a mild overexpression (less than a 35% increase) of the human tau.
findings.evidence: Comparison of human MAPT transgene expression against endogenous mouse tau quantified the degree of overexpression, used to argue that native-promoter models avoid gross overexpression confounds.
findings.effect_size: <35% increase in tau over endogenous mouse tau
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The wildtype genomic human MAPT transgene is under its native promoter control [9], and when compared to wildtype mouse tau, we only observed a mild overexpression (less than a 35% increase) of the human tau.
findings.study_system: Transgenic mouse expressing wild-type human MAPT under its native promoter

findings.claim: Cross-species mapping of motor cortex cell types shows that SST interneuron subtypes are among the least conserved between mouse and human, with within-species classifier performance collapsing across species, and SST-expressing cells occupying different laminar positions in human versus mouse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Distinct consensus types such as ChC and Sst-Chodl were more robust (mean area under the receiving operating characteristic (AUROC) curve = 0.99 within species, 0.88 across species) than were closely related types such as Sncg and Sst subtypes (mean AUROC = 0.84 within species, 0.50 across species).
findings.evidence: Single-nucleus transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of M1 in mouse, marmoset, macaque and human; MetaNeighbour cross-species cluster matching quantified conservation per cell type.
findings.effect_size: Sst subtype cross-species AUROC = 0.50 (chance) vs 0.84 within species
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Distinct consensus types such as ChC and Sst-Chodl were more robust (mean area under the receiving operating characteristic (AUROC) curve = 0.99 within species, 0.88 across species) than were closely related types such as Sncg and Sst subtypes (mean AUROC = 0.84 within species, 0.50 across species).
findings.study_system: Mouse, marmoset, macaque and human primary motor cortex, single-nucleus transcriptomics

findings.claim: Decreased brain pH and increased lactate occur in mouse models of psychiatric disease that have no medication exposure, indicating that pH/lactate shifts reported in human postmortem brain are not purely agonal or medication artefacts but can reflect disease biology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also observed increased lactate levels in the brains of model mice, as well as a highly significant negative correlation between pH and lactate levels, consistent with the findings of previous human postmortem studies (Halim et al, 2008).
findings.evidence: Brain pH and lactate were measured in multiple drug-naive mouse models and compared with the human postmortem literature, isolating the contribution of confounders that cannot be controlled in human tissue.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: significant negative pH-lactate correlation in model mice
findings.study_system: Mouse models of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and autism spectrum disorder; brain tissue pH and lactate

findings.claim: Core intrinsic excitability mechanisms of parvalbumin interneurons are conserved between human and mouse neocortex despite quantitative differences in input resistance, indicating that species divergence is not uniform across interneuron properties.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Fig. 1 Proportional decreases in input excitability during membrane hyperpolarization are conserved between human and mouse parvalbumin (Pvalb) neurons despite differences in Rin. a Identification of Pvalb interneurons in neocortical layer 2/3.
findings.evidence: Patch-clamp recordings from layer 2/3 Pvalb interneurons in human and mouse neocortex with Ba2+ block of Kir channels showed the same proportional change in input resistance in both species.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: conserved proportional decrease in Rin despite species difference in absolute Rin
findings.study_system: Human and mouse neocortical layer 2/3 parvalbumin interneurons, patch-clamp

findings.claim: Conclusions about disease modifiers in Alzheimer's research rest almost entirely on APP-overexpressing mouse models whose non-physiological promoters make APP processing unlike the human situation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In addition, the mouse models use the neuron-specific Thy1-promotor to overexpress the N-terminal truncated Aβ species, which makes APP processing even less similar to the human situation.
findings.evidence: The authors surveyed the model base used for peripheral-inflammation studies and noted that all rely on APP/PS1 overexpression driven by heterologous promoters.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: all prior studies used APP-overexpressing models
findings.study_system: Review/experimental study of amyloid mouse models (APP-overexpressing transgenics)

findings.claim: Interneuron vulnerability differs between human Alzheimer postmortem tissue and transgenic mouse models, and between subpopulations, so model-derived vulnerability rankings do not transfer directly to human disease.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Data from different authors and our previous results indicate a differential interneuron vulnerability in postmortem tissue from Alzheimer's patients and in transgenic mice model (Fonseca and Soriano, 1995; Solodkin et al., 1996; Brady and Mufson, 1997; Leuba et al., 1998; Iritani et al.,
findings.evidence: Comparison of olfactory bulb interneuron populations in APP/PS1 mice with the human postmortem literature; somatostatin- and calretinin-positive cells decreased while parvalbumin cells increased.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: SST and calretinin decreased, parvalbumin increased in APP/PS1 olfactory bulb
findings.study_system: APP/PS1 transgenic mouse olfactory bulb, compared with human Alzheimer postmortem literature

findings.claim: AppNL/NL knock-in mice accumulate insoluble amyloid-beta but show negligible behavioural and glial phenotypes, demonstrating that cognitive deficits seen in overexpressing transgenics are not a necessary consequence of amyloid burden.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Accordingly, we found no changes in number and reactivity of microglial cells in old AppNL/NL mice compared to WT (n = 4) (Fig. 1E).
findings.evidence: Behavioural testing and glial quantification in aged AppNL/NL knock-in mice found no genotype differences in locomotion, anxiety-related measures or microglial reactivity despite increased insoluble amyloid-beta.
findings.effect_size: no change in microglial number/reactivity (n = 4); no difference in speed or distance travelled
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Accordingly, we found no changes in number and reactivity of microglial cells in old AppNL/NL mice compared to WT (n = 4) (Fig. 1E).
findings.study_system: AppNL/NL knock-in mouse model of Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: Behavioural findings in App knock-in models have failed to replicate between laboratories, and overexpression in conventional transgenics is explicitly flagged as a source of artificial phenotypes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For instance, while in the original report, deficits in the Y-maze were indicated19, a later study did not find deficits in working memory using the Y-maze at 6 months of age22.
findings.evidence: The authors document a direct replication discrepancy for Y-maze working memory in App knock-in mice between the original report and a later study at the same age.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: Y-maze deficit reported originally, absent in later study at 6 months
findings.study_system: App knock-in mouse model of Alzheimer's disease; in vivo electrophysiology and behaviour

findings.claim: Every existing TDP-43 nuclear-localisation-signal mouse model carries technical limitations that prevent faithful reproduction of patient pathology, including Cre-lox strategies that produce disease-irrelevant splicing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While various TDP-43 NLS mice models have been developed to date, each has specific technical limitations in closely mirroring the patient pathology.
findings.evidence: A survey of TDP-43 mislocalisation models identified construct-specific artefacts, including Cre-lox deletion of RNA-recognition-motif exons producing ALS-irrelevant alternative splicing.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: all existing models carry construct-specific limitations
findings.study_system: TDP-43 knock-in and transgenic mouse models of ALS/FTD

findings.claim: Transgene insertion in widely used tauopathy mouse lines disrupts endogenous genes at the integration site, so phenotypes attributed to the human transgene may partly reflect insertional mutagenesis.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In detail, human tau cDNA disrupted the first exons and promoter regions of fibroblast growth factor 14 (Fgf14) and CamK2a promoter-tetracycline activator transgene in Tg(CamK2a-tTA)1Mmay mice (CamK2a-tTA tg mice) (Mayford et al., 1996) disrupted Vipr2, Wdr60, Esyt2, D430020J02Rik, Ncapg2 and Ptprn2
findings.evidence: Genomic characterisation of tau transgenic lines identified specific endogenous genes disrupted by the transgene integration; suppressing P301L tau from ~13x to ~3x endogenous levels reversed behavioural deficits while tangles continued to accumulate.
findings.effect_size: transgene disrupts Fgf14 plus 6 genes at the CamK2a-tTA locus; P301L tau expressed at ~13x endogenous levels
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Interestingly, suppression of P301L tau expression with doxycycline from ~13 times to ~3 times endogenous levels in rTg4510 mice reversed behavioral impairments in these mice although NFTs continued to increase, suggesting that NFTs were unlikely to be the initial neurotoxic species (
findings.study_system: Human tau-expressing transgenic mouse lines (rTg4510, CamK2a-tTA)

findings.claim: Brain tissue pH and RNA integrity number exert gene-set-specific effects on postmortem expression data, with pH affecting cell-cycle genes and RIN affecting RNA-processing genes, so unadjusted postmortem comparisons confound disease signal with tissue quality.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also recently investigated the effects of pH and RIN on gene expression levels using microarray gene expression data for the postmortem brain tissues of 13 patients with schizophrenia and found that pH strongly affected genes related to the cell cycle, RIN strongly affected genes related to RNA p
findings.evidence: Microarray expression data from postmortem brain were regressed against pH and RIN, revealing distinct and substantial pathway-level contributions of each tissue-quality variable.
findings.effect_size: pH and RIN each drive distinct gene-set-level expression effects (n = 13 postmortem brains)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We also recently investigated the effects of pH and RIN on gene expression levels using microarray gene expression data for the postmortem brain tissues of 13 patients with schizophrenia and found that pH strongly affected genes related to the cell cycle, RIN strongly affected genes related to RNA p
findings.study_system: Human postmortem brain tissue (schizophrenia brain bank cohort)

findings.claim: Neuropeptides degrade rapidly after death unless enzymes are inactivated by in vivo heat stabilisation, so neuropeptide measurements such as somatostatin in conventionally collected postmortem tissue are vulnerable to postmortem loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Among in vivo fixation techniques, focused microwave irradiation (FMW) to the brain, by which the tissues are rapidly heated to 85°C–95°C, was developed to irreversibly deactivate enzymes, preventing postmortem degradation of neurotransmitters and neuropeptides (Balcom et al. 1975; Blank et al. 1979
findings.evidence: Comparison of heat-stabilised and conventionally handled brain tissue by mass spectrometry imaging showed preserved neuropeptide signals without delocalisation when enzymes were heat-inactivated.
findings.effect_size: heat stabilisation at 85-95 degrees C prevents postmortem neuropeptide degradation
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among in vivo fixation techniques, focused microwave irradiation (FMW) to the brain, by which the tissues are rapidly heated to 85°C–95°C, was developed to irreversibly deactivate enzymes, preventing postmortem degradation of neurotransmitters and neuropeptides (Balcom et al. 1975; Blank et al. 1979
findings.study_system: Rodent brain tissue, mass spectrometry imaging of neuropeptides with and without heat stabilisation

findings.claim: Cross-species single-cell comparison of cortical inhibitory neurons requires an investigator-supplied homology mapping and identifies at least one mouse-specific inhibitory class absent from human data, limiting direct transfer of interneuron taxonomies between species.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Using the inhibitory neuron homology provided by the investigators (Hodge et al. 2019), we combined the subclass of the data sets into five major cell types: LAMP5+, VIP+, SST+, PVALB+, and MEIS2+, where MEIS2+ is a mouse-specific cell type that was not detected in the human data.
findings.evidence: A cross-species cell-type assignment method was benchmarked on 54 scRNA-seq datasets spanning seven species; inhibitory subclass mapping between human and mouse depended on a manually curated homology table.
findings.effect_size: MEIS2+ inhibitory class present in mouse but not detected in human data
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Using the inhibitory neuron homology provided by the investigators (Hodge et al. 2019), we combined the subclass of the data sets into five major cell types: LAMP5+, VIP+, SST+, PVALB+, and MEIS2+, where MEIS2+ is a mouse-specific cell type that was not detected in the human data.
findings.study_system: Human and mouse cortical single-cell RNA-seq datasets (54 datasets, 7 species)

findings.claim: Endogenous APP is not uniformly expressed across cell types but is enriched in GABAergic interneurons in mouse hippocampus, which undermines the assumption that pan-neuronal transgenic overexpression reproduces the native cellular distribution of amyloid precursor protein.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Contrary to the long-held perception that APP is a ubiquitously expressed protein, regional and cell-type specific differences of endogenous APP expression, including a striking expression pattern in GABAergic interneurons, have been observed in the mouse hippocampus by us and others [28, 31].
findings.evidence: Cell-type-resolved analysis of endogenous APP expression and Abeta secretion identified GABAergic interneurons as disproportionate contributors, contrasting with the uniform-expression assumption built into overexpression models.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: APP enriched in GABAergic interneurons rather than ubiquitously expressed
findings.study_system: Mouse hippocampus; human iPSC-derived neuron cultures (cited comparison)

findings.claim: Immunolabelling for somatostatin, parvalbumin and other GABAergic markers was indistinguishable between transgenic and knock-in Huntington's disease mice and wild type, despite the transgenics showing prominent nuclear inclusions.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Immunolabeling for calbindin D 28K, enkephalin, substance P, glutamic acid decarboxylases (M(r) 65,000 or 67,000, GAD65 and GAD67), somatostatin, choline acetyltransferase, parvalbumin, and glial fibrillary acidic protein were remarkably similar in transgenic, knock-in, and wild-type mice.
findings.evidence: Parallel comparison of a transgenic fragment model and a knock-in model found enkephalin mRNA decreases without changes in peptide/enzyme immunolabelling or DNA damage, dissociating inclusion pathology from marker loss.
findings.effect_size: no detectable difference in somatostatin or parvalbumin immunolabelling between genotypes
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Immunolabeling for calbindin D 28K, enkephalin, substance P, glutamic acid decarboxylases (M(r) 65,000 or 67,000, GAD65 and GAD67), somatostatin, choline acetyltransferase, parvalbumin, and glial fibrillary acidic protein were remarkably similar in transgenic, knock-in, and wild-type mice.
findings.study_system: Transgenic and knock-in mouse models of Huntington's disease, striatum and cortex

findings.claim: GABAergic interneuron marker mRNAs including somatostatin decline differentially with age in rat hippocampus and inversely track upregulation of the alpha1 GABA-A receptor subunit, indicating marker-level change without demonstrated cell loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There was a differential age-related decrease in these interneuronal mRNAs that was inversely correlated with up-regulation of the alpha1 GABA receptor subunit.
findings.evidence: Quantitative mRNA measurement of GAD65/67, parvalbumin, calretinin, somatostatin, NPY and VIP in young versus old rat hippocampus.
findings.effect_size: differential age-related decrease in interneuronal mRNAs, inversely correlated with alpha1 subunit upregulation
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: There was a differential age-related decrease in these interneuronal mRNAs that was inversely correlated with up-regulation of the alpha1 GABA receptor subunit.
findings.study_system: Young and aged rat hippocampus, mRNA quantification

findings.claim: In aged rat hippocampus both somatostatin mRNA and the number of somatostatin-immunopositive cells decline while parvalbumin interneuron numbers are preserved, showing that interneuron vulnerability is subtype-selective rather than global.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The mRNA expression of somatostatin, a neuropeptide expressed by some GABAergic interneurons, and the number of somatostatin-immunopositive cells decreased in aged rats.
findings.evidence: Parallel measurement of somatostatin mRNA and immunopositive cell counts in the same aged animals, with parvalbumin counts as an internal comparison, addresses whether marker mRNA loss tracks cell loss.
findings.effect_size: decreased SST mRNA and SST+ cell number; parvalbumin cell number preserved
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: However, the number of hippocampal parvalbumin-containing GABAergic interneurons was preserved.
findings.study_system: Aged rat hippocampus

findings.claim: Ndnf-expressing interneuron excitability is spared in a Dravet syndrome mouse model, contradicting the generalised interneuron hypothesis that all GABAergic subclasses depend on Nav1.1 for action potential generation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This has been shown for three of the major subclasses of cerebral cortex GABAergic INs: those expressing parvalbumin (PV), somatostatin, and vasoactive intestinal peptide.
findings.evidence: Patch-clamp characterisation of a fourth interneuron subclass in the same model that showed deficits in PV, SST and VIP cells provides a within-model negative control for the interneuron hypothesis.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: Ndnf interneuron excitability unaffected while PV/SST/VIP are affected
findings.study_system: Dravet syndrome (Scn1a) mouse model, cortical Ndnf interneurons

findings.claim: Combined immunolabelling, calcium imaging and chemogenetics in pilocarpine temporal lobe epilepsy mice show that a large Dlx-expressing interneuron population survives but becomes hypoactive, separating survival from functional impairment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To address this issue, we combined immunolabeling, calcium imaging, electrophysiology, chemogenetic tools, and behavioral assays in mouse pilocarpine TLE models to investigate the survival and changes in the activity of a large population of Dlx-expressing interneurons and test the effect of their m
findings.evidence: Dlx-based labelling captures interneurons independent of neuropeptide marker expression, so survival estimates are not confounded by marker downregulation.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: interneurons survive but are hypoactive
findings.study_system: Pilocarpine mouse model of temporal lobe epilepsy, hippocampal Dlx-expressing interneurons

findings.claim: A narrative synthesis frames early excitation-inhibition imbalance in Alzheimer's disease as driven by either loss or dysfunction of PV and SST interneurons, leaving the loss-versus-dysfunction distinction unresolved in the primary literature.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This narrative review synthesises pre-clinical and clinical data showing how disruption of excitation-inhibition balance, driven chiefly by the loss or dysfunction of parvalbumin- and somatostatin-positive GABAergic interneurons (INs), emerges early in AD and fosters subclinical epileptiform activit
findings.evidence: A review-level synthesis that treats loss and dysfunction as interchangeable drivers, illustrating how the ambiguity propagates through the secondary literature.
findings.study_system: Narrative review of preclinical and clinical Alzheimer's disease literature

findings.claim: Quantitative analysis of 15 whole-brain human postmortem specimens including pathologic Alzheimer's disease cases characterises white matter interstitial neurons, a population routinely omitted from cortical interneuron counts.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Here, we investigated 15 whole-brain human postmortem specimens, including cognitively normal cases and those with pathologic Alzheimer's disease (AD).
findings.evidence: Quantitative and qualitative measurement of neuronal size, density and relation to vasculature across whole-brain postmortem specimens.
findings.effect_size: 15 whole-brain postmortem specimens
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Here, we investigated 15 whole-brain human postmortem specimens, including cognitively normal cases and those with pathologic Alzheimer's disease (AD).
findings.study_system: Human whole-brain postmortem specimens, cognitively normal and pathologic Alzheimer's disease

findings.claim: After kainate-induced seizures 63% of hilar somatostatin-immunoreactive neurons survived at the septal end of the hippocampus, indicating partial rather than complete loss of this population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Kainate-induced seizures caused a loss of hilar somatostatin-immunoreactive neurons in the septal end of the hippocampus, where 63% of the somatostatin-immunoreactive neurons survived.
findings.evidence: Regional counts of somatostatin-immunoreactive hilar neurons along the septotemporal axis after kainate treatment.
findings.effect_size: 63% of SST-immunoreactive hilar neurons survived
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Kainate-induced seizures caused a loss of hilar somatostatin-immunoreactive neurons in the septal end of the hippocampus, where 63% of the somatostatin-immunoreactive neurons survived.
findings.study_system: Kainate-treated rat hippocampal hilus

findings.claim: In naturally occurring hippocampal sclerosis in sea lions, somatostatin-immunoreactive axons were exuberant in the dentate gyrus despite loss of immunopositive hilar neurons, dissociating somatic marker loss from axonal marker expression.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Similar to human patients, hippocampal sclerosis in sea lions was unilateral in 79% of cases, mossy fiber sprouting was a common neuropathological abnormality, and somatostatin-immunoreactive axons were exuberant in the dentate gyrus despite loss of immunopositive hilar neurons.
findings.evidence: Neuropathological survey of a naturally occurring, non-engineered animal model of hippocampal sclerosis, compared against human temporal lobe epilepsy features.
findings.effect_size: unilateral sclerosis in 79% of cases; SST+ axons exuberant despite SST+ hilar somatic loss
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Similar to human patients, hippocampal sclerosis in sea lions was unilateral in 79% of cases, mossy fiber sprouting was a common neuropathological abnormality, and somatostatin-immunoreactive axons were exuberant in the dentate gyrus despite loss of immunopositive hilar neurons.
findings.study_system: California sea lion hippocampus with naturally occurring hippocampal sclerosis

findings.claim: A composite presynaptic index combining GAD67 and SST mRNA alterations was reduced in 80.4% of individuals with schizophrenia, showing that pooling correlated marker transcripts raises detection sensitivity relative to single-marker comparisons in postmortem cohorts.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A presynaptic index of dendritic inhibition, derived by summing the alterations in GAD67 and SST mRNAs, was lower in 80.4% of individuals with schizophrenia and was associated with final educational attainment (adjusted odds ratio = 1.44, p = .022).
findings.evidence: Postmortem transcript quantification across a case-control cohort with a composite index, reporting the proportion of affected individuals rather than only group means.
findings.effect_size: index lower in 80.4% of cases; adjusted odds ratio 1.44, p = 0.022
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A presynaptic index of dendritic inhibition, derived by summing the alterations in GAD67 and SST mRNAs, was lower in 80.4% of individuals with schizophrenia and was associated with final educational attainment (adjusted odds ratio = 1.44, p = .022).
findings.study_system: Human postmortem prefrontal cortex, schizophrenia case-control cohort

findings.claim: Glutaminyl cyclase is expressed in overlapping subsets of parvalbumin-, calbindin-, calretinin-, cholecystokinin- and somatostatin-positive interneurons, so neurochemical marker categories are not mutually exclusive populations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Hippocampal QC-immunoreactive neurons include subsets of parvalbumin-, calbindin-, calretinin-, cholecystokinin- and somatostatin-positive GABAergic interneurons.
findings.evidence: Double-labelling of glutaminyl cyclase against five interneuron markers across postnatal development showed partial overlap with each.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: QC overlaps with five interneuron marker classes
findings.study_system: Rodent hippocampus across postnatal development

findings.claim: APP overexpression produces memory impairment even without amyloid deposition in some transgenic lines, so behavioural phenotypes in overexpressing models cannot be attributed to amyloid-beta and may reflect APP-fragment biology irrelevant to Alzheimer's pathogenesis.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Moreover, overexpression of APP causes memory impairment without Aβ deposition in some App transgenic mice [8, 11], suggesting that the brains of these transgenic mouse models may have pathophysiological properties that are not relevant to AD pathogenesis.
findings.evidence: The authors motivate the App knock-in approach by documenting that overexpression generates excess APP fragments, confounding attribution of phenotypes to amyloid-beta.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: memory impairment without amyloid deposition in some APP-overexpressing lines
findings.study_system: App knock-in and APP-overexpressing transgenic mouse models, behavioural testing

findings.claim: In hippocampus, the widely used SST-IRES-Cre driver crossed to a tdTomato reporter labels a substantial fraction of cells that do not express SST mRNA, with specificity lowest in the CA3 pyramidal cell layer, so Cre-reporter counts overestimate the SST population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that in these experiments, the SST-IRES-Cre mouse line is nonspecific in CA3, with only 48/127 (37.8%) tdTomato + cells being SST-mRNA + in the PCL, 82/100 (82%) in SO and 61/74 (82.4%) in SR ( Figures 6A–C ).
findings.evidence: Single-molecule mRNA in situ hybridisation for SST was combined with Cre-dependent tdTomato labelling and scored cell-by-cell across CA3 laminae; the same laboratory showed that a different interneuron-targeting line was far more specific in the same preparation, so the failure is line-specific rather than a staining artifact.
findings.effect_size: Only 48/127 (37.8%) tdTomato+ cells in CA3 pyramidal cell layer were SST-mRNA+; 82% in stratum oriens and 82.4% in stratum radiatum
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found that in these experiments, the SST-IRES-Cre mouse line is nonspecific in CA3, with only 48/127 (37.8%) tdTomato + cells being SST-mRNA + in the PCL, 82/100 (82%) in SO and 61/74 (82.4%) in SR ( Figures 6A–C ).
findings.study_system: SST-IRES-Cre;tdTomato reporter mice, hippocampal CA3/CA1

findings.claim: Cre-driver lines used to target a defined brain cell class show sporadic recombination in non-target cells throughout the brain, and the degree of this leakage differs between nominally equivalent lines and between studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: It is unclear why the leakage into neurons varies among the different Cx3cr1-cre lines and studies ( Parkhurst et al., 2013 ; Hwang et al., 2017 ; Zhang et al., 2018 ; Zhao et al., 2018 ), but the problem has raised concerns about whether there is a reliable cre-line that targets microglia with good specificity.
findings.evidence: Reporter crosses were examined brain-wide and non-target labelled cells were counted; the authors note the inconsistency across published characterisations of the same driver family, which is the generic failure mode for interpreting Cre-based cell-type ablation or manipulation experiments.
findings.effect_size: Several dozen non-microglial GFP-positive cells scattered throughout the brain (qualitative count)
findings.study_system: Cx3cr1-Cre driver lines crossed to fluorescent reporters, mouse brain

findings.claim: Most widely used amyloid models overexpress APP to generate pathology, and a knock-in design was adopted specifically so that amyloid-driven proteome changes could be measured without the artifacts introduced by APP overexpression.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This enabled us to analyze the effects of enhanced Aβ 42 levels in the brain over time without the artifacts caused by overexpressing AβPP.
findings.evidence: A longitudinal proteomic comparison of App knock-in versus wild-type cortex and hippocampus at multiple ages; the authors state the overexpression artifact as the motivation for the design and report that few individual proteins overlapped between time points even within the same model.
findings.effect_size: Few proteins overlapped between time points despite pathway-level convergence (qualitative)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Although only a few proteins overlapped between the time points, many of the differently expressed proteins at 3 and 6 months of age are involved in similar biological pathways, for instance neuron/brain development, cytoskeletal dynamics/remodeling, synaptic function, and vesicular transport.
findings.study_system: App NL-F/NL-F knock-in vs wild-type mice, cortex and hippocampus proteome

findings.claim: Commercially available interneuron Cre-driver strains including Sst-Cre are maintained on a C57BL/6 background carrying the Cdh23 age-related hearing-loss allele, so sensory decline confounds age-related phenotypes attributed to the labelled interneuron population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: But there is an important limitation: in the majority of commercially available Cre strains, the Cre gene is carried on a C57BL/6 background.
findings.evidence: Auditory brainstem response thresholds were measured across ages in Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre lines and compared with background strains; the authors document the Cdh23-dependent hearing-loss phenotype as a property of the background rather than of the Cre insertion.
findings.effect_size: Age-related hearing loss detectable at high frequencies by 2-3 months and severe by 6 months in C57BL/6-background strains
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our findings confirm previous work suggesting AHL is first detectable at high frequencies by 2–3 months old, and progressively worsens with age such that thresholds are severely elevated at high frequencies by 6 months old, and across all frequencies by 12 months old.
findings.study_system: Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mouse lines, auditory brainstem responses

findings.claim: Within a single App knock-in line, behavioural readouts of the same construct gave opposite interpretations across tasks, illustrating that model phenotypes are assay-dependent rather than stable properties of the genotype.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Within the current study, we observed a conflicting phenotype between increased thigmotaxis in the OF (anxiogenic) and increased time in the open arms in the EPM (anxiolytic).
findings.evidence: Multiple behavioural assays plus diffusion MRI were run in the same cohort; the authors explicitly flag the contradiction between open-field and elevated-plus-maze results in their own data.
findings.effect_size: Increased thigmotaxis in open field (anxiogenic) versus increased open-arm time in elevated plus maze (anxiolytic) in the same mice
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Within the current study, we observed a conflicting phenotype between increased thigmotaxis in the OF (anxiogenic) and increased time in the open arms in the EPM (anxiolytic).
findings.study_system: AppNL-G-F knock-in mice, behaviour and diffusion tensor imaging

findings.claim: Homologous cortical interneuron types are present in human and mouse but differ in both relative abundance and gene expression, including substantial divergence within SST subtypes, so mouse interneuron data cannot be transferred to human cortex quantitatively.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Again, we found similar proportions of MGE (50.2 ± 2.3%) and CGE (44.2 ± 2.4%) interneurons in human, and >2 times as many MGE (67.8 ± 0.9%) than CGE (30.8 ± 1.2%) interneurons in mouse.
findings.evidence: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of human middle temporal gyrus and mouse cortex were mapped to homologous types and quantified by in situ validation; the imbalance of MGE versus CGE interneurons differs by roughly twofold between species, and marker gene expression diverges by more than tenfold within matched types.
findings.effect_size: Human: 50.2 +/- 2.3% MGE vs 44.2 +/- 2.4% CGE interneurons; mouse: 67.8 +/- 0.9% MGE vs 30.8 +/- 1.2% CGE; 18% of genes in the Sst Chodl type >10-fold divergent
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Again, we found similar proportions of MGE (50.2 ± 2.3%) and CGE (44.2 ± 2.4%) interneurons in human, and >2 times as many MGE (67.8 ± 0.9%) than CGE (30.8 ± 1.2%) interneurons in mouse.
findings.study_system: Human middle temporal gyrus and mouse cortex, single-nucleus RNA-seq

findings.claim: Adult-onset expression of human APP produces region-specific hyperexcitability rather than a uniform effect, so phenotypes attributed to amyloid in transgenic models depend on where and when the human transgene is expressed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Here we show that the entorhinal cortex is more prone to hyperexcitability, with respect to the somatosensory cortex, following adult-onset expression of the human amyloid precursor protein (hAPP).
findings.evidence: Human APP or tau expression was induced in adulthood in a region-restricted manner and compared between entorhinal and somatosensory cortex in the same animals, separating intrinsic regional vulnerability from the construct itself.
findings.effect_size: Entorhinal cortex more prone to hyperexcitability than somatosensory cortex under identical adult-onset hAPP expression (qualitative)
findings.study_system: Mice with adult-onset region-specific human APP or tau expression, entorhinal vs somatosensory cortex

findings.claim: Neuron-number estimates for the same brain structure in the same species differ substantially between investigators using the same stereological method, so cross-study comparisons of interneuron counts carry methodological variance that is comparable to the biological effects being claimed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While estimates obtained with the IF vary by around 15% across groups for the same species, which is in the range of biological variation, different investigators using the same stereological method on the same species and brain structures report estimates that often are more than 100% different ( Table 1 ).
findings.evidence: A direct methodological comparison of the isotropic fractionator and design-based stereology quantified both within-method inter-investigator spread and between-method agreement, and analysed the sources of counting error including the number of particles counted per estimate.
findings.effect_size: Isotropic fractionator estimates vary by about 15% across groups for the same species, within the range of biological variation, while the same stereological method applied by different investigators to the same structure diverges more
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: While estimates obtained with the IF vary by around 15% across groups for the same species, which is in the range of biological variation, different investigators using the same stereological method on the same species and brain structures report estimates that often are more than 100% different ( Table 1 ).
findings.study_system: Methodological comparison of cell-counting approaches in rodent and human brain

findings.claim: Postmortem interval has a measurable effect on RNA integrity in human brain tissue, with the proportion of usable samples falling sharply once the interval exceeds about five hours, so cohorts differing in postmortem interval differ systematically in molecular measurability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also found a definite difference in RIN between autopsies with PMI greater or less than 5 hours as 96% of samples from our shorter-PMI autopsies had RIN greater than or equal to 7.5 vs only 74% of those from the longer-PMI autopsies (p < 0.05).
findings.evidence: RNA integrity numbers were compared between autopsies stratified by postmortem interval within one brain bank and against published cohorts with longer intervals; the brain bank's short median interval was associated with a higher proportion of usable samples.
findings.effect_size: 96% of samples from autopsies with PMI <5 h had RIN >=7.5 versus 74% from longer-PMI autopsies; 87% of samples met criterion at median PMI 3.5 h (p < 0.001 versus comparison cohort)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We also found a definite difference in RIN between autopsies with PMI greater or less than 5 hours as 96% of samples from our shorter-PMI autopsies had RIN greater than or equal to 7.5 vs only 74% of those from the longer-PMI autopsies (p < 0.05).
findings.study_system: Human postmortem brain bank tissue, RNA integrity and gene expression

findings.claim: An App knock-in rat was developed because existing knock-in mice lack overt neurodegeneration, and the rat model showed progressive brain atrophy, indicating that the absence of neuron loss in mouse knock-ins is partly a species limitation rather than evidence against amyloid-driven degeneration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: First, this new model with appropriate timing of pathologies opens up real opportunities to study how aging leads or affects neurodegeneration.
findings.evidence: The same humanised App knock-in alleles were introduced into rat; brain weight and behavioural measures were tracked longitudinally and compared with the published mouse knock-in phenotype.
findings.effect_size: Overall brain weight loss of 9.11% at 12 months and 16.09% at 22 months in homozygous App knock-in rats
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Quantitative analysis revealed an overall brain weight loss of 9.11% and 16.09% in 12- and 22-month-old homozygous rats, respectively (Supplementary information, Fig.
findings.study_system: App NL-G-F knock-in rats versus wild-type rats

findings.claim: Two amyloid mouse models analysed with identical stereological methods in the same study gave opposite results for hippocampal interneuron number, with losses in the plaque-bearing line and no change in the intraneuronal-amyloid line.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We observed significantly reduced numbers of CR- and PV-positive cells in the hippocampus of plaque-bearing 5XFAD mice; however, no significant alterations compared with WT were measured in the Tg4-42 mouse model.
findings.evidence: Calretinin- and parvalbumin-positive neurons were counted in 5XFAD and Tg4-42 mice against wild-type controls in one laboratory with one protocol, and the authors checked that the reductions exceeded what hippocampal volume loss could explain.
findings.effect_size: About 30% reduction in calretinin-positive and more than 40% in parvalbumin-positive neurons in 5XFAD; no significant alteration in Tg4-42
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: However, the observed reduction of CR- and PV-positive neuron numbers of ∼30% for CR- and more than 40% for PV-positive cells suggests that volume loss alone is not sufficient to explain this observation.
findings.study_system: 5XFAD and Tg4-42 mouse models, hippocampal interneuron stereology

findings.claim: Transgene integration in APP-overexpressing mouse lines can destroy endogenous loci, and the authors argue that every overexpression line in current use should be whole-genome sequenced before its phenotypes are interpreted as amyloid effects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We suggest that all transgenic mouse models being used in research in which APP or APP/PSEN1 are overexpressed should undergo whole genome sequencing (WGS) so that destroyed loci that possibly affect their phenotypes can be identified ( Sasaguri et al., 2017 ).
findings.evidence: A methodological review comparing first-generation overexpression lines with App knock-in models, including side-by-side immunohistochemistry of APP and synaptic markers in knockout, wild-type, overexpressing and knock-in mice.
findings.effect_size: Recommendation that all APP/PSEN1-overexpressing transgenic lines undergo whole genome sequencing to identify disrupted loci (qualitative)
findings.study_system: Review and comparison of APP overexpression versus App knock-in mouse models

findings.claim: In cortical slice electrophysiology, between-animal variance accounted for a third to a half of the total variance in synaptic charge measures, so studies with few animals can report group differences that reflect animal sampling rather than genotype or treatment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The absence of significance in the phasic I charge analysis may be caused by the large variance among subgroups, i.e., among different animals (31.98% and 52.83% of total variance, Es and Is, respectively), as well as within subgroups, i.e., among different cells (53.15% and 44.70% of total variance, Es and Is, respectively).
findings.evidence: Spontaneous synaptic events were decomposed by variance component across animals and cells and compared with conventional group tests in the same dataset, showing which negative results were attributable to inter-animal spread.
findings.effect_size: Inter-animal variance 31.98% and 52.83% of total variance for excitatory and inhibitory charge respectively
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The absence of significance in the phasic I charge analysis may be caused by the large variance among subgroups, i.e., among different animals (31.98% and 52.83% of total variance, Es and Is, respectively), as well as within subgroups, i.e., among different cells (53.15% and 44.70% of total variance, Es and Is, respectively).
findings.study_system: Mouse cortical pyramidal neurons, spontaneous synaptic event analysis

findings.claim: RNA integrity in postmortem human brain varied with both diagnosis and brain region in Alzheimer's disease but not in Huntington's or Parkinson's disease, so tissue quality is itself a disease-dependent variable that can masquerade as a disease effect in expression studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Simple main effects analysis showed that in AD, both disease ( p = 0.0350) and region ( p = 0.0142) had a statistically significant effect on RIN.
findings.evidence: RIN was measured across matched regions and diagnoses within the same brain bank and analysed with disease and region as factors, so the AD-specific effect could be separated from generic autopsy variation.
findings.effect_size: AD: significant effects of disease (p = 0.0350) and region (p = 0.0142) on RIN; HD caudate normal 7.125 vs HD 6.9 (p = 0.808); PD substantia nigra 6.44 vs 6.73 (p = 0.6006)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Simple main effects analysis showed that in AD, both disease ( p = 0.0350) and region ( p = 0.0142) had a statistically significant effect on RIN.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem brain tissue, multiple regions, AD/HD/PD versus controls

findings.claim: Automated application of the physical disector in a fractionator design improves the quality and throughput of neuron counts relative to manual implementations, indicating that published count differences partly reflect which stereological implementation a laboratory could afford to run.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, with a slightly larger initial expenditure of effort, the quality and quantity of the stereological analyses can be improved substantially by applying an automated physical disector principle in a fractionator design for quantitative analysis of immunophenotyped neurons.
findings.evidence: The automated physical disector was benchmarked against conventional counting in lesioned and intact tissue, with parallel volume estimates showing the magnitude of the structural change being measured.
findings.effect_size: Ipsilateral substantia nigra pars compacta volume reduced 27% (4.80 +/- 0.32 vs 6.60 +/- 0.27 mm3) in one series and 59% (0.64 +/- 0.20 vs 1.58 +/- 0.22 mm3) in another
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Volume estimates showed a reduction in ipislateral SNc volume by 27% (4.80 + 0.32 mm 3 ), as compared to the corresponding contralateral SNc volume (6.60 ± 0.27 mm 3 ) (data not shown).
findings.study_system: Rodent substantia nigra, stereological method comparison

findings.claim: The relative abundance of calcium-binding-protein and neuropeptide-defined interneuron classes in homologous brain regions differs between rodents, monkeys and humans, so marker-defined interneuron categories are not interchangeable across species.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our results in the human and chimpanzee suggest the opposite, since, CR-ir neurons represented the most evident CBP-positive category.
findings.evidence: The same antibody panel was applied to matched regions of several species in one laboratory, with antibody epitope conservation checked across species, isolating biological species differences from reagent differences.
findings.effect_size: Calretinin-immunoreactive neurons were the most prominent calcium-binding-protein category in human and chimpanzee, the opposite of the rodent pattern; densities differed across all three species
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among the three species we noted a difference in the density of the neurons expressing the CaBPs (Table 2 ).
findings.study_system: Human, chimpanzee/monkey and rodent brain, immunohistochemistry for calcium-binding proteins and neuropeptides

findings.claim: Cre-driver lines nominally targeting the same population differ in the spatiotemporal pattern of recombinase activity, and these differences alone are sufficient to produce divergent phenotypes from the same floxed allele.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the spatiotemporal differences in Cre recombinase activity would lead to divergent phenotypes.
findings.evidence: Three widely used driver lines were crossed to the same reporter and their embryonic recombination patterns compared directly, isolating driver identity as the variable.
findings.effect_size: Divergent phenotypes attributed to spatiotemporal differences in Cre activity between three lines (qualitative)
findings.study_system: Emx1-IRES-Cre, D6-Cre and hGFAP-Cre mouse lines crossed to reporter mice

findings.claim: A GFP transgenic line widely used as a proxy for SST interneurons labels fewer than half of the SST-positive cells in layer II/III and about a third in deeper layers, so conclusions drawn from such lines apply to a biased subset of the SST population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We showed that GIN cells account for 44% of the SST+ interneurons in layer II/III and around 35% in layers IV and Va.
findings.evidence: GFP-labelled cells were counted against SST immunolabel layer by layer and their marker co-expression profiled, quantifying both the coverage and the composition bias of the line.
findings.effect_size: GIN cells are 44% of SST+ interneurons in layer II/III and about 35% in layers IV and Va; 29% of GIN cells co-express calretinin (54% in layer II/III)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We showed that GIN cells account for 44% of the SST+ interneurons in layer II/III and around 35% in layers IV and Va.
findings.study_system: GIN (GFP-expressing inhibitory neuron) transgenic mouse neocortex

findings.claim: In human App knock-in mice, entorhinal parvalbumin interneurons became hypoexcitable while neighbouring excitatory neurons became hyperexcitable at an age with no cell loss, showing that early interneuron phenotypes are functional and region-specific rather than degenerative.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In entorhinal cortex, amyloid overproduction resulted in parvalbumin interneuron hypoexcitability, whereas excitatory neurons were concurrently hyperexcitable.
findings.evidence: Semi-automated patch-clamp recordings sampled large numbers of identified cells across regions in young knock-in mice, so opposite changes in two populations were measured in the same slices.
findings.effect_size: Over 150 cells recorded in 2-month-old mice; PV interneuron hypoexcitability with concurrent excitatory neuron hyperexcitability in entorhinal cortex
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We designed and employed a semi-automated patch clamp electrophysiology apparatus to record from fast-spiking parvalbumin interneurons and excitatory neurons in these regions, recording from over 150 cells in 2 month old amyloid precursor protein knock-in (APP-KI) mice.
findings.study_system: Human App knock-in mice, entorhinal cortex and comparison region, patch-clamp electrophysiology

findings.claim: Baseline interneuron marker levels differ between mouse strains that also differ in susceptibility to a neurotoxic insult, so strain background sets the starting point against which interneuron loss in any disease model is measured.
findings.claim_source_sentence: C57BL/6J mice, for instance, are more susceptible to MPTP-induced Parkinsonism whereas CD-1 mice are resistant.
findings.evidence: Striatal and nigral interneuron marker proteins were quantified in two untreated strains with documented differences in MPTP susceptibility, establishing the baseline contribution before any lesion.
findings.effect_size: C57BL/6J mice more susceptible to MPTP-induced parkinsonism than resistant CD-1 mice, with differing baseline interneuronal protein levels; striatal interneurons comprise only 5-10% of striatal cells
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: C57BL/6J mice, for instance, are more susceptible to MPTP-induced Parkinsonism whereas CD-1 mice are resistant.
findings.study_system: C57BL/6J and CD-1 mouse strains, striatum and substantia nigra interneuron markers

findings.claim: In human Alzheimer piriform cortex, somatostatin- and calretinin-positive cells were preferentially reduced while parvalbumin cells were not, locating the vulnerability in specific marker-defined populations rather than in GABAergic neurons generally.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results indicated preferential vulnerability of somatostatin- (p = 0.0001 < α = 0.05) and calretinin-positive (p = 0.013 < α = 0.05) cells that colocalized with amyloid-β peptide, while the prevalence of parvalbumin-positive cells was increased (p = 0.045 < α = 0.05) in the Alzheimer's cases.
findings.evidence: Interneuron marker counts were combined with amyloid and tau labelling in the same sections from ten Alzheimer cases, so vulnerability was assessed against local pathology rather than against a global disease label.
findings.effect_size: Somatostatin p = 0.0001 and calretinin p = 0.013 for preferential vulnerability; parvalbumin prevalence not comparably affected
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Results indicated preferential vulnerability of somatostatin- (p = 0.0001 < α = 0.05) and calretinin-positive (p = 0.013 < α = 0.05) cells that colocalized with amyloid-β peptide, while the prevalence of parvalbumin-positive cells was increased (p = 0.045 < α = 0.05) in the Alzheimer's cases.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem piriform cortex, Alzheimer's disease cases

findings.claim: In an APP/PS1 mouse the olfactory cortex showed temporal changes in interneuron populations with SST cells heavily co-localised with amyloid, a model counterpart to the human piriform findings that nonetheless depends on transgenic amyloid overproduction.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In addition, double-labeling experiments indicated high levels of co-localization of SST-positive cells with amyloid-β expression in olfactory areas.
findings.evidence: Interneuron populations were counted across ages in the same transgenic line and correlated with amyloid deposition, providing the time course that cross-sectional human material cannot supply.
findings.effect_size: High co-localization of SST-positive cells with amyloid-beta expression in olfactory areas (qualitative, double labelling)
findings.study_system: AbetaPP/PS1 double-transgenic mice, olfactory cortex interneuron populations

findings.claim: In Huntington's disease cortex somatostatin immunoreactivity was increased in a minority of areas rather than decreased, and striatal lesions in rats produced no cortical peptide changes, so cortical peptide alterations in the human disease are not a secondary consequence of striatal degeneration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We studied the same cortical peptides in rats with long-standing striatal lesions and found no significant changes of CCK-LI, NPY-LI, VIP-LI, or SRIF-LI in any of the 8 cortical regions that were examined.
findings.evidence: The same peptide panel was measured in human HD cortex and in rats with long-standing striatal lesions; the animal experiment functions as a direct test of the secondary-degeneration explanation for the human result.
findings.effect_size: Cholecystokinin elevated 57-153% in HD cortex; somatostatin increased in only 3 areas; no significant peptide changes in any of 8 cortical regions of lesioned rats
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concentrations of immunoreactive cholecystokinin (CCK-LI) were consistently elevated 57 to 153% in HD cortex.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem Huntington's disease cortex and rats with striatal lesions

findings.claim: Brain pH was lower in Alzheimer cases than controls and correlated positively with measurable mRNA for nearly every gene examined, so disease-associated transcript reductions in postmortem cortex are partly explained by agonal and tissue-state variables rather than by cell loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Mean brain pH was significantly lower in AD (6.4) than in control subjects (6.5, ANOVA, p<0.01), though there was no difference between male and females of either group.
findings.evidence: mRNA abundance for multiple genes was related to pH, postmortem interval, age and sex within the same case series, showing the pH dependence held across pathology and sex groupings.
findings.effect_size: Mean brain pH 6.4 in AD versus 6.5 in controls (ANOVA p < 0.01); positive pH-mRNA correlations for all genes except GFAP
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Mean brain pH was significantly lower in AD (6.4) than in control subjects (6.5, ANOVA, p<0.01), though there was no difference between male and females of either group.
findings.study_system: Human postmortem brain, quantitative mRNA measurement across diagnostic groups

findings.claim: In an autopsy series of rapidly progressive dementia, concomitant pathologies were present in nearly three-quarters of cases and clinicopathological diagnostic agreement outside prion disease was poor, quantifying how far a clinical diagnosis label misrepresents the tissue used in postmortem cohorts.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We observed clinicopathological diagnostic agreement in 94% of the patients with prion RPD but only in 21% of those with non-prion RPD.
findings.evidence: Clinical diagnoses were compared case by case against full neuropathological examination, and co-pathologies were enumerated in the same series, so both the misclassification rate and the mixed-pathology rate come from one cohort.
findings.effect_size: Diagnostic agreement 94% for prion versus 21% for non-prion rapidly progressive dementia; concomitant pathologies in 117 of 160 cases (73%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concomitant pathologies were detected in 117 (73%).
findings.study_system: Human autopsy cohort, rapidly progressive dementia

findings.claim: Systematic testing of commercial antibodies used for brain immunohistochemistry showed that standard validation tests do not establish specificity, so published maps of marker-defined neuronal populations can reflect antibody behaviour rather than antigen distribution.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These results showed that great caution needs to be exercised when interpreting the results of brain immunohistochemistry using CB₂ receptor antibodies and that, in general, none of the tests for antibody validity that have been proposed, apart from the knockout control test, are reliable.
findings.evidence: Multiple antibodies against the same target were compared in brain tissue alongside the usual validation controls, and the authors show which controls fail to discriminate specific from non-specific labelling.
findings.effect_size: None of the tested antibody-validity criteria was sufficient to establish specificity for brain immunohistochemistry (qualitative)
findings.study_system: Brain immunohistochemistry, commercial receptor antibodies, validation testing

findings.claim: Frozen brain sections shrink to roughly a quarter of their cut thickness along the z-axis with section-to-section variability, which biases optical-disector neuron counts unless measured thickness is used, a correction not applied uniformly across the interneuron-counting literature.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In the z-axis (perpendicular to the cutting surface), however, sections shrink to ∼25% of the cut thickness.
findings.evidence: Section thickness was measured directly in frozen sections and the within- and between-section variability quantified, giving the magnitude of the error introduced by assuming nominal thickness.
findings.effect_size: z-axis shrinkage to about 25% of cut thickness; between-section coefficient of variation about 10%, within-section about 3%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This z-axis shrinkage was quite variable between sections (coefficient of variation about 10%) but stable within the same section (coefficient of variation about 3%).
findings.study_system: Frozen brain sections, stereological thickness measurement

findings.claim: Stereology in a triple-transgenic line overexpressing mutant APP, presenilin-2 and tau showed degeneration of GABAergic septo-hippocampal projection neurons and their hippocampal interneuron targets, a positive loss result obtained in exactly the overexpression context that knock-in studies identify as artifact-prone.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Stereological analysis of TauPS2APP mice revealed significant neurodegeneration of GABAergic septo-hippocampal projection neurons as well as their target cells, the GABAergic hippocampal interneurons.
findings.evidence: Unbiased stereological counts were combined with marker mRNA measurement and field-potential recording in the same line, so the reported loss is anchored to both molecular and functional readouts; cholinergic septal neurons in the same sections were unaffected.
findings.effect_size: Degeneration dependent on hippocampal subfield and interneuron subtype, with dentate gyrus and NPY-positive interneurons most strongly affected; cholinergic medial septum neurons unaffected
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Moreover, the degeneration of hippocampal GABAergic interneurons was dependent on the hippocampal subfield and interneuronal subtype investigated, whereby the dentate gyrus and the NPY-positive interneurons, respectively, were most strongly affected.
findings.study_system: TauPS2APP triple-transgenic mice, medial septum and hippocampus, stereology

findings.claim: Human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived MGE interneurons grafted into brain develop almost exclusively into SST and PVALB subtypes, providing a human-cell system in which SST interneuron properties can be studied without relying on cross-species inference from mouse lines.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Comparative transcriptomics against endogenous human brain datasets revealed that 97% of grafted cells developed into somatostatin (SST) and parvalbumin (PVALB) subtypes, including populations that exhibit selective vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
findings.evidence: Grafted cells were profiled by comparative transcriptomics against endogenous human brain reference datasets, so subtype assignment is made on a human reference rather than a mouse taxonomy.
findings.effect_size: 97% of grafted cells developed into SST and PVALB subtypes
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Comparative transcriptomics against endogenous human brain datasets revealed that 97% of grafted cells developed into somatostatin (SST) and parvalbumin (PVALB) subtypes, including populations that exhibit selective vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
findings.study_system: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived MGE interneurons grafted in vivo, comparative transcriptomics

arg_01.thesis: Measurement decides the answer - Present the quantitative core: reported SST change spans zero to roughly 37-55% loss, and denominator and labelling strategy covary systematically with magnitude - reporter fate mapping and stereology small or null, immunoreactivity counts in chemoconvulsant models large. Add the ageing control: transcript falls by half or more in aged rodent brain with no demonstrated cell loss, so any comparison that is not tightly age-matched can mistake ageing for disease.
arg_01.synthesis: Subsection 1 of 6. Anchored on 3 pre-extracted cross-study comparison(s); 4 findings in this package carry the anchored metrics directly. Remaining support for this subsection is drawn from arg_unanchored.

arg_02.thesis: Genetic access is neither complete nor specific - Quantify tool error in both directions - reporter-positive non-SST cells and SST cells never labelled - and show it differs by line and region, which matters because disease phenotypes are reported per line without this correction. Distinguish specificity from coverage and refuse to plot them on one axis.
arg_02.synthesis: Subsection 2 of 6. Anchored on 1 pre-extracted cross-study comparison(s); 3 findings in this package carry the anchored metrics directly. Remaining support for this subsection is drawn from arg_unanchored.

arg_03.thesis: Construct and dosage as a predictor of phenotype - Show that model classes span more than an order of magnitude in transgene dosage, from physiological knock-in to roughly 13x endogenous tau, and that reducing dosage can reverse a behavioural phenotype while pathology accumulates - making dosage the proximate cause of some reported interneuron phenotypes.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell loss versus marker downregulation for SST interneurons in human Alzheimer's disease cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No study in the retrieved set applies a marker-independent identification of human SST interneurons (for example in situ hybridisation for SST transcript combined with a pan-GABAergic or nuclear-identity readout in the same tissue) to decide whether reduced SST immunoreactivity in human AD cortex reflects fewer cells or lower per-cell expression. The reporter-based dissociations all come from mouse and rat models.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The entire clinical interpretation of SST loss - whether it is a degenerative endpoint or a reversible expression state - rests on this distinction, and it is currently settled only in rodents.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Effect of postmortem interval and agonal state specifically on somatostatin peptide and transcript
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Quantitative dose-response data for somatostatin peptide and SST mRNA as a function of postmortem interval, brain pH and agonal duration in human tissue. Available evidence is either general (pH and RIN affecting gene sets) or from rodent tissue with heat stabilisation.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Human SST deficits in dementia are reported from tissue with heterogeneous postmortem handling, and without a somatostatin-specific degradation curve the reported effect sizes cannot be corrected or bounded.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Quantified off-target recombination in Sst-Cre lines across brain regions and ages
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: The retrieved evidence quantifies Sst-Cre PV overlap in a single region (presubiculum) in one study. There is no systematic, region-by-region and age-by-age audit of Sst-Cre fidelity, and no audit at all under neurodegenerative conditions where SST expression itself changes.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: If SST expression falls in disease, Cre expression history and current marker status diverge, so the same driver line can behave differently in disease and control tissue - a confound that would systematically bias every Sst-Cre experiment in a disease model.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental source for the claim that SST interneurons are the earliest and most vulnerable interneuron population in Alzheimer's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - the claim is repeated across reviews and introductions in the retrieved set (for example the excitation-inhibition review and the alpha5-GABA-A preprint) but those statements cite secondary literature rather than a traceable primary quantification.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated claim whose original data source is not identifiable from the reviews that assert it, and which the negative stereological results in amyloid rodent models directly contradict.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Replication of App knock-in behavioural phenotypes across laboratories
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Multi-site or pre-registered replication of cognitive phenotypes in App knock-in lines. The retrieved set contains a documented non-replication of a Y-maze deficit and a report of negligible deficits alongside a report of cognitive and emotional alterations, with no arbitrating study.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Interneuron dysfunction in these models is usually interpreted against a behavioural phenotype; if the phenotype itself is unstable between laboratories, the circuit-level interpretation inherits that instability.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direct comparison of SST interneuron number between APP-overexpressing and App knock-in lines in the same laboratory
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: No retrieved study counts SST interneurons in an overexpression line and a knock-in line side by side with one protocol, one age series and one observer; the overexpression-versus-knock-in discrepancy is currently inferred across laboratories and decades
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The central model-validity claim of this literature — that interneuron loss is an overexpression artifact — rests on cross-study comparison, which is exactly the inference that the counting-method variance literature says is unreliable

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Quantified fidelity of Sst-Cre driver lines in diseased tissue
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Reporter specificity and coverage for SST lines have been measured only in healthy animals; no retrieved study re-measures the fraction of reporter-positive cells expressing Sst after amyloid, tau or polyglutamine pathology, when Sst transcription itself may change
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Fate-mapping arguments that distinguish marker downregulation from cell death assume reporter labelling is disease-independent; if Cre expression or recombination efficiency shifts with pathology, the control is circular

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental source for the claim that somatostatin interneurons are the most vulnerable interneuron class in Alzheimer's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration with marker-independent identification — the ordering of interneuron class vulnerability is repeated across reviews, but the retrieved primary studies disagree about parvalbumin and measure SST by immunoreactivity, which confounds peptide level with cell presence
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated ranking of interneuron vulnerability without a traceable marker-independent experimental source

conflict_atlas_all_90.paper_a_claim: Our data furthermore highlight more similarities than differences between L2/3 and L5 inhibitory networks: e.g. the strength of the Pvalb-Pvalb and Sst-Pvalb connections, and the lack of Sst-Sst and of Pvalb-Sst connections are comparable across these two layers.

conflict_atlas_all_90.nature_of_conflict: Whether Sst interneurons form recurrent Sst→Sst connections: paired recordings in mouse V1 slices reported a lack of Sst-Sst connections in L2/3 and L5, whereas large-scale multipatch recordings in mouse and human neocortex observed Sst-Sst connections in every layer (with Patch-seq confirmation of 5/66 probed pairs). Differences in Cre-line specificity (Sst-IRES-Cre labels some Pvalb-like fast-spiking cells), sampling scale, and detection sensitivity may contribute; SOM-SOM disinhibition during cooperative recruitment (10.1016/j.neuron.2016.02.037) supports the existence of functional Sst-Sst inhibition.

The dimension of disagreement is laminar/subtype-specific target selection (Martinotti vs non-Martinotti L4-targeting SST cells).

conflict_atlas_all_90.nature_of_conflict: Morphological identity of layer 4 SST interneurons: one study reports that L4-targeting SOM+ cells constitute a single non-Martinotti population, whereas paired-recording work finds L4 SST cells to be non-Martinotti in somatosensory cortex but Martinotti-like in visual cortex. conflict_atlas_all_90.paper_a_claim: Although a modest trend toward larger EPSPs was observed in sPCs at higher stimulation intensity under CNO, paired comparison at maximal stimulation intensity revealed no significant change in EPSP area (Fig. , left).

Conclusions

Continuous fornix DBS disrupts physiological bidirectional communication within the FX-HC network, which may underlie the limited efficacy seen in clinical trials.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
